steps.what: Buy and sell jewelry or represent buyers and sellers through assessment, negotiation and agreement

tasks.design: Retain buying, selling and brokerage with the jeweler. A customer record or invoice template does not replace transaction judgement and negotiation.
tasks.previous_blocker: The transaction depends on the object, price, trust and the parties' intentions.
tasks.enabler_now: No supplied evidence establishes replacement of this relationship and judgement work.
tasks.still_hard: Judge whether an offer is appropriate and explain its conditions.
tasks.human_edge: Assess the object and negotiate a mutually understood agreement.
tasks.altitude: Improve the clarity and evidence behind transaction decisions.

reach.learn: Separate a customer's stated preference from an acceptable agreement

evidence.claim: Jewellery transaction judgement and negotiation remain human work; no task specific labour saving is established.

assumptions: The jeweler obtains and checks object and party information during s1; no free authenticity, value or acceptable offer flag is assumed.
Invoice production and customer record maintenance are not invented as baselines for this selling task.
No new system is deployed, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Transaction type, mandate and current process
research_questions: Which misunderstandings most often prevent a clear transaction agreement?

already_counted.description: Object assessment, party discussion and negotiation

incremental.description: No added software or operating work

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100: buying, selling and brokerage remain fully human; zero gross and net savings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Verify gemstone identity, grade evidence and appraisal basis and capture price guide lookup criteria
Retrieve price guide rows matching the verified gemstone criteria
Determine appraised values using guide evidence, market fluctuations, rarity and professional judgement

tasks.design: Use the guide's native search or a licensed table lookup in {SPREADSHEET}, with evidence retained in {DOCS}. Lookup returns source rows rather than an appraisal; the jeweler determines value and its limitations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Comparable guide entries may need repeated manual searching.
tasks.enabler_now: Native filters can retrieve exact matches from a current, licensed structured guide.
tasks.still_hard: Interpret grade, rarity and changing market conditions for the appraisal purpose.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise that a nominally matching guide entry does not establish the object's value.
tasks.altitude: Own valuation assumptions and source traceability.

reach.learn: Distinguish a guide quote from an appraisal

evidence.claim: Exact filters can retrieve supplied guide rows without making a gemstone appraisal; guide availability and labour savings are E1 model knowledge.

assumptions: In s1 the jeweler verifies and captures stone identity, relevant grade fields, weight and units, appraisal purpose, comparison criteria and guide edition. Inspection, evidence checking, entry and missing detail clarification are counted in 30 hours.
The guide publisher produces dated structured price rows through the existing licensed supply process; native search is used before any custom export. No free manually curated price table is assumed.
Missing fields, unavailable licensed rows or uncertain grade equivalence stop automated lookup and return to manual source review in s3.
Market context is obtained and assessed by the jeweler in s3; no machine market adjustment, authenticity flag or final value is inferred.
No saving is assigned to the professional appraisal itself or to selling the object.
unknowns: Licensed guide search and export availability
Time spent searching versus evaluating evidence
research_questions: Does native guide lookup save time after grade verification and professional interpretation?

already_counted.description: Stone and grade verification, criterion capture and value determination

incremental.description: Guide edition checks and sampled lookup reconciliation
Licensed guide access and table support

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 task scenarios: B=100, R=75 gives 25 gross and 17 net after 8 focal upkeep hours. Range 0-4 allows existing guide search, uncertain comparability and retained appraisal judgement.

role.altitude: Use traceable guide retrieval to support valuation while retaining object assessment and transaction judgement.
reach: Help retail colleagues explain the limits of guide prices
role.ambitious_version: A jeweler who can trace price evidence quickly and still owns every appraisal and negotiated transaction.
